note: Task #103: real memory-pressure test with model-specific-profile-selected layers, 360M, ctx=180000, real GTX 1650 (Vulkan), the same known Phase 11B/11C boundary. --capacity-only mode (single candidate context, no F16 reference) to avoid risking a real OOM while probing right at the boundary. Quality-at-boundary is NOT measured here (same disclosed limitation as Phase 11C's pressure_boundary.json) -- this answers only the memory question.

provenance.membrane_commit: see git log for experiment/model-specific-mixed-policy HEAD at artifact time

real_byte_constants_at_ctx_180000.derived_from: all_q5 (32*bq5=2764800000) and all_q8 (32*bq8=3916800000) capacity-only runs at this exact ctx -- these differ substantially from the ctx=2048 constants (835584/589824 for 135M scale, 1392640/983040 for 360M) since KV bytes scale with context size

results.source: reproducibility recheck of the same config

results.failure_stage: compute buffer allocation (ggml_gallocr_reserve_n_impl), not the KV tensor allocation itself

results.source: membrane_memory_budget_policy at budget=3.4e9 bytes (real ctx=180000 constants) -- theoretically well under the all-Q8 total of 3.9168e9

real_boundary_found.reproducible: profile_top8_q8 config re-run once more (profile_top8_q8_recheck) with identical result

findings: The model-specific profile's own top-8 layer selection sits EXACTLY at this host's real GPU memory boundary at ctx=180000 -- it succeeds, and adding even one more Q8 layer (top-9, only 36MB more theoretical KV bytes, <1% of the all-Q8 total) fails. This is a razor-thin real margin, not a big safety cushion.

Theoretical KV-byte totals alone do NOT reliably predict allocation success this close to the boundary: the memory-budget-policy-selected 17-layer config (3.3768e9 bytes) has a theoretical byte total comfortably below the all-Q8 total (3.9168e9 bytes, ~14% headroom) yet still fails to allocate -- because the real constraint near this boundary is the COMBINED KV + compute-buffer + driver-overhead footprint, not KV bytes in isolation. membrane_memory_budget_policy's pure byte-budget math (Task #99) is exact for KV bytes specifically but does not, and was never claimed to, account for this additional non-KV allocation overhead.

The failure MODE itself changes with layer count: 12+ Q8 layers fail at the KV tensor allocation step (ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory), while 9-10 Q8 layers fail one step later, at compute-buffer allocation (ggml_gallocr_reserve_n_impl) -- both are real, cleanly-reported failures (no crash, no silent fallback, context_creation_succeeded correctly reported as false in both cases), but they are two different resource pools running out, which is itself informative for anyone trying to build a safety margin on top of this.

Compared to Phase 11C's own earlier 8-layer pressure_boundary.json test (which used a differently-derived 8-layer set, '1,13,18,19,22,23,25,30'), this phase's TRAIN21-derived profile selects a very similar but not identical set ('1,13,18,19,23,24,25,30' -- differs only in layer 22 vs 24), and both succeed at this exact boundary -- consistent, not contradictory, evidence.
conclusion: The model-specific profile's layer selection is confirmed to work at the real, known 360M ctx=180000 memory-pressure boundary on real Vulkan/GTX 1650 hardware, at exactly the same 8-layer budget Phase 11C already established as safe. The margin above that point is far tighter than pure theoretical byte math suggests, which is a real, disclosed constraint on how aggressively any future memory-budget policy could push toward the all-Q8 boundary without an explicit non-KV overhead margin.
